title: How to Study for CFA Level 1: A 6-Month Plan for Working Students & Freshers
excerpt: The CFA Institute suggests candidates plan for roughly 300 hours of study per level. That number scares people until they divide it: 300 hours across 26 weeks is about 11–12 hours a week. That is two focused hours on weekdays and a solid weekend block. This plan shows you how to spend those hours wisely….
description: Follow a 26-week CFA Level 1 study plan built for freshers and working professionals: weekly hours, topic order, mock exams and online vs classroom tips.
content:
The CFA Institute suggests candidates plan for roughly 300 hours of study per level. That number scares people until they divide it: 300 hours across 26 weeks is about 11–12 hours a week. That is two focused hours on weekdays and a solid weekend block. This plan shows you how to spend those hours wisely.

Know the Exam Before You Plan

Level I is a multiple-choice exam. Recent formats use 180 questions across two sessions. Because CFA Institute updates formats, windows and eligibility rules, confirm the current details on its website before you register.

The curriculum covers ten topic areas:

  1. Ethical and Professional Standards
  2. Quantitative Methods
  3. Economics
  4. Financial Statement Analysis
  5. Corporate Issuers
  6. Equity Investments
  7. Fixed Income
  8. Derivatives
  9. Alternative Investments
  10. Portfolio Management

Topics carry different weights. Ethics, Financial Statement Analysis, Equity and Fixed Income typically carry the largest shares, so give them proportionally more time. Check the latest weightings on the CFA Institute site.

Who This Plan Is For

  • Freshers and final-year students who can study 12–15 hours a week
  • Working professionals who can study about 10–12 hours a week, with extra time in the final month

The plan assumes zero finance background. If you already hold a commerce degree, you may move faster through Accounting and Economics.

The 26-Week Plan

Start Ethics early with short weekly reviews, then return to it intensively. The topic rewards repetition.

A Weekly Rhythm for Working Students

  • Monday to Thursday: 1.5–2 hours each evening. Read one chapter section and solve questions on it.
  • Friday: Rest or a 30-minute flashcard review.
  • Saturday: 4–5 hours. Complete the week’s remaining reading and a timed question set.
  • Sunday: 2–3 hours. Review mistakes and update your formula sheet.

Block your calendar like a meeting, because “whenever I find time” usually means never.

The Study Method That Works

Use a three-step loop for every topic:

  1. Learn: Read or watch the lesson once with full attention.
  2. Apply: Solve practice questions immediately.
  3. Review: Log every wrong answer and write why you missed it.

Question practice matters more than re-reading. In our experience supporting candidates, those who solve questions from week 2 onwards retain far more than those who read first and practise later.

Calculator and Formula Skills

CFA allows approved calculators only, so learn yours early. Practise time value of money, statistics and bond functions until they are automatic. Keep a one-page formula sheet for each topic and revise it every Sunday.

Mock Exams: Your Final Eight Weeks

From roughly week 18, start mixing mixed-topic question sets. In weeks 24–25, attempt at least three to four full mock exams under real timing. After each one:

  • review every wrong answer and every lucky guess,
  • tag mistakes as concept, calculation or reading errors, and
  • revisit weak topics within 48 hours.

Online vs Classroom: How to Choose

Both formats work, so match the format to your life.

When you compare a CFA Level 1 online course or CFA online coaching, ask about live doubt sessions, recorded access, mock exam analysis and faculty credentials. For Mumbai students who prefer in-person discipline, EdgeX Learning runs a CFA course in Mumbai with structured classes, mock exams, a practice question bank and regular doubt-solving sessions. You can also explore our CFA classes in Mumbai page for course details.

Common Mistakes to Avoid

  • Ignoring Ethics until the end. Study it throughout.
  • Reading without practising. Questions reveal what you actually know.
  • Skipping mocks. They train stamina and timing.
  • Burning out in month two. Consistency beats intensity.
  • Choosing a date before you check readiness. Pick your exam window, then confirm that your mock scores support it.

Is CFA the Right Choice for You?

CFA suits careers in investment research, portfolio management and markets. If you are still weighing options against CA or ACCA, our CFA vs CA vs ACCA guide will help. Because the field is changing fast, also read our article on whether AI will replace accountants to see which complementary skills matter.

Frequently Asked Questions

How many hours do I need to study for CFA Level 1?

CFA Institute suggests planning around 300 hours. Many candidates spend more if they are new to finance.

Can I study for CFA Level 1 while working full-time?

Yes. Plan 10–12 hours a week for about six months, and protect your weekend blocks.

Is six months enough for CFA Level 1?

For most disciplined candidates, yes. Freshers without finance exposure may want seven or eight months.

What is the CFA Level 1 passing score?

CFA Institute does not publish a fixed passing percentage; it sets a minimum passing score for each exam. Aim to score comfortably above 70% in your mock exams as a safety margin.

Which topic should I study first?

Start with Quantitative Methods and Economics, because they underpin later topics, and revisit Ethics weekly.

Is a CFA online course enough, or do I need classroom coaching?

Either can work. Choose the format that gives you the accountability and doubt support you need.

Who is eligible to register for CFA Level 1?

Candidates generally need to hold, or be in the final year of, a bachelor’s degree, or have relevant professional experience. Confirm current rules with CFA Institute.

title: Will AI Replace Accountants? What CA, ACCA & CFA Students Should Learn Now
excerpt: A client uploads 2,000 invoices at 9 AM. By 9:05, software has read, categorised and matched them. Ten years ago, that was a junior team’s week. So, will AI replace accountants? The honest answer has two parts. AI will replace many tasks accountants do today. It will not replace the need for accountable, qualified professionals….
description: Will AI replace accountants? See which tasks AI automates, which roles stay human and the data, AI and judgment skills CA, ACCA and CFA students should build now.
content:
A client uploads 2,000 invoices at 9 AM. By 9:05, software has read, categorised and matched them. Ten years ago, that was a junior team’s week. So, will AI replace accountants?

The honest answer has two parts. AI will replace many tasks accountants do today. It will not replace the need for accountable, qualified professionals. The difference between those two statements decides your career, and this guide shows you how to land on the right side of it.

What AI Already Does Well in Accounting

AI and automation excel at work that is repetitive, rule-based and high-volume. Today they handle:

  • Data entry and invoice processing: reading documents and posting entries
  • Bank and ledger reconciliations: matching transactions at scale
  • First-draft reporting: summarising trial balances and variances
  • Anomaly detection: flagging unusual transactions for review
  • Routine queries: answering standard compliance or policy questions

Therefore, entry-level roles built purely on data processing face the most pressure. Students who plan to rely only on these tasks should rethink their path.

What AI Cannot Do (Yet)

AI struggles where the work needs judgment, accountability and trust:

  • Professional judgment: interpreting a grey area in tax law or an accounting standard
  • Accountability: a signed audit opinion or tax filing needs a qualified human who bears responsibility
  • Ethics and scepticism: challenging management’s explanations
  • Client relationships: explaining a complex decision, negotiating and advising
  • Context: understanding a business’s strategy, risks and people

Regulators and clients still require qualified professionals to take responsibility for outcomes. A model can draft; a CA, ACCA member or CFA charterholder must decide and sign.

Role by Role: Who Is Affected and How?

These ratings reflect the general direction of the profession, not a fixed forecast. Pace varies by employer, sector and country.

Does This Change How You Choose CA, ACCA or CFA?

Not the qualification itself, but how you use it. Professional bodies are responding. ACCA’s 2027 redesign, for instance, adds a paper with a data-analysis focus and stronger technology themes, as we explain in our ACCA 2027 changes guide. Meanwhile, CFA’s curriculum already emphasises quantitative reasoning, and CA training builds the audit and tax depth that clients still pay for. If you are still choosing, our CFA vs CA vs ACCA comparison helps you decide.

The Skills to Learn Now

1. Advanced Excel and Data Handling

Master pivot tables, lookups, Power Query and clean data practices. Excel remains the daily tool of finance, and AI tools plug directly into it.

2. Data Visualisation (Power BI or Tableau)

Learn to turn numbers into a story a manager understands in one minute.

3. SQL and Basic Python

You do not need to become a developer. However, basic SQL and Python let you extract and analyse data without waiting for IT. These count among the most practical data science skills for accountants.

4. AI Literacy and Prompting

Learn how large language models work, where they hallucinate and how to verify their output. The professional who can test and challenge an AI answer becomes more valuable, not less.

5. Controls, Ethics and Data Privacy

As firms adopt AI, they need people who understand risk, documentation and confidentiality. Ethical judgment is a core professional skill in every one of these qualifications.

6. Communication and Advisory Skills

Practise explaining a number, a risk or a recommendation in plain language. Tools produce reports; professionals produce decisions.

A Simple 90-Day Upskilling Plan

Study 4–5 hours a week alongside your exams. Because the skills reinforce your syllabus, they save time rather than steal it.

What Employers Look For

In practice, hiring managers increasingly ask for the same combination: a recognised qualification, comfort with data tools and sound judgment. Showing a small project, such as a reconciliation automated in Excel or a dashboard you built, often impresses more than a certificate alone.

Where to Build These Skills

Syllabus preparation and skill-building should run in parallel. EdgeX Learning supports students with CA classes in Mumbai, ACCA coaching in Mumbai and a CFA course in Mumbai. Book counselling to ask how each programme builds data and Excel skills alongside the syllabus, so your qualification and your toolkit grow together. If you are preparing for CFA, our Level 1 study plan shows how to fit extra learning around a working schedule.

The Bottom Line

AI will remove tasks, change entry-level roles and raise expectations. It will also create demand for professionals who can govern, interpret and challenge machine output. Accountants who learn to work with AI will not be replaced by it; they will replace colleagues who refuse to adapt.

Frequently Asked Questions

Will AI replace accountants by 2030?

AI will automate many routine accounting tasks by then, but regulation, accountability and judgment keep qualified professionals essential. Expect role changes rather than disappearance.

Will AI replace CAs in India?

AI will change how CAs work, especially in compliance, reconciliation and research. Statutory roles such as audit and certifications still need a human professional who signs and takes responsibility.

Is ACCA still worth it with AI?

Yes, particularly because ACCA’s 2027 changes add data and technology skills. Pair the qualification with practical analytics skills.

Which skills should an accountant learn for the AI era?

Excel, data visualisation, SQL or Python basics, AI literacy, ethics and communication.

Can AI do my tax return or audit?

AI can prepare drafts and flag issues, but a qualified professional must review, decide and sign off.

What are the best AI tools for accountants?

Common categories include AI features inside Excel and accounting software, document-extraction tools and general AI assistants. Always check data privacy before uploading client information.

Is accounting still a good career?

Yes. The routine work shrinks, but demand for analysis, advisory, assurance and finance leadership remains strong.

title: CFA vs CA vs ACCA: Which Finance Qualification Should You Choose?
excerpt: Which one is best?” is the wrong question. The right question is: which one fits the career you want in the next ten years? CFA vs CA vs ACCA, overlap in name recognition but differ sharply in focus, structure and where they open doors. This guide compares them honestly, so you can choose with clarity…
description: cfa vs ca vs acca on career paths, difficulty, duration, global value and fit. Find the right finance qualification for you in 2026–27.
content:
Which one is best?” is the wrong question. The right question is: which one fits the career you want in the next ten years? CFA vs CA vs ACCA, overlap in name recognition but differ sharply in focus, structure and where they open doors.

This guide compares them honestly, so you can choose with clarity rather than peer pressure.

The 30-Second Answer

  • Choose CA if you want a career in Indian audit, taxation, compliance or finance leadership with strong domestic recognition.
  • Choose ACCA if you want global accounting, audit, reporting or finance roles, with flexible exam sittings and recognition across many countries.
  • Choose CFA if you want to work in investments: equity research, portfolio management, asset management or investment banking.

What Each Qualification Is

CA (Chartered Accountant)

ICAI conducts the CA course in India. The route includes Foundation, Intermediate and Final levels, plus practical training (articleship). CA holds statutory authority in India for roles such as statutory audit and certain certifications, which makes it central to Indian practice.

ACCA (Association of Chartered Certified Accountants)

ACCA is a global professional body. Its qualification currently has 13 exams, and from 2027 it moves to a restructured model of 11 exams. It also requires relevant practical experience for membership. You can read more in our guide to the ACCA 2027 changes.

CFA (Chartered Financial Analyst)

The CFA Institute offers the CFA programme in three levels. It focuses on investment analysis, ethics and portfolio management, and it requires relevant work experience before you can earn the charter. Level I is multiple-choice, and the later levels add case-based formats.

Side-by-Side Comparison

Verify fees, eligibility and duration with each body, because they change often and vary by route.

Difficulty: How Do They Really Compare?

Each course is hard in a different way.

  • CA: Heavy syllabus, written exams, long preparation and a demanding practical-training phase.
  • ACCA: Many exams, but spread across sittings; consistency matters more than marathon study.
  • CFA: A broad, deep curriculum tested through MCQs; CFA Institute suggests candidates plan around 300 hours of study per level.

None is “easy”. Therefore, choose the one whose difficulty matches your strengths. If you enjoy writing detailed answers and law, CA fits. If you prefer structured modules and flexibility, ACCA fits. If you enjoy markets and quantitative analysis, CFA fits.

Career Paths and Salary Reality

Salaries vary by city, employer, experience and skill, so ignore any blog that promises a fixed number. Instead, compare roles:

  • CA: Statutory audit, tax advisory, GST and compliance, internal audit, CFO pipeline in Indian companies.
  • ACCA: Multinational finance teams, Big Four audit, financial reporting, management accounting, overseas roles.
  • CFA: Equity research, asset management, wealth management, risk and investment banking.

AI and automation are reshaping all three, and the strongest candidates pair their qualification with data skills. Our article on whether AI will replace accountants explains which skills to build.

Can You Combine Them?

Yes, and many professionals do. A CA with a CFA gains investment credentials; an ACCA member can add CFA for a markets pivot. However, avoid starting two heavy courses at once. Finish one, then add another if your career needs it.

Which Should You Choose? A Quick Decision Guide

Ask yourself:

  1. Where do I want to work? India-centred practice points to CA; global mobility points to ACCA or CFA.
  2. What work excites me? Audit and tax lean CA; reporting and finance leadership lean ACCA; markets lean CFA.
  3. How do I prefer to study? Large written syllabus suggests CA; modular suggests ACCA; MCQ-driven suggests CFA.
  4. What are my time and budget limits? Compare total cost and duration, not only the first exam.

Studying in Mumbai: What to Look For

Mumbai has strong coaching options for all three. Whichever you pick, evaluate faculty experience, batch size, test practice and placement or career guidance. EdgeX Learning offers CA classes in Mumbai, ACCA coaching in Mumbai and a CFA course in Mumbai, so you can discuss all three options with one counsellor rather than hearing a single-course pitch. If CFA appeals to you, read our 6-month CFA Level 1 study plan.

Frequently Asked Questions

Which is better, CFA, CA or ACCA?

None is universally better. CA suits Indian audit and tax, ACCA suits global accounting careers and CFA suits investment careers.

Is ACCA equal to CA?

They differ in scope and recognition. CA carries statutory authority in India, while ACCA offers broader international recognition.

Which is the toughest among CFA, CA and ACCA?

Each is demanding in its own way. CA is the longest and most written-exam intensive; CFA is broad and MCQ-heavy; ACCA tests consistency across many papers.

Can I do CFA after CA or ACCA?

Yes. Many professionals add CFA to move into investment roles.

Which is best after 12th commerce?

CA Foundation, ACCA and CFA (after graduation or in the final year of a degree, per CFA Institute rules) are all possible. Choose based on career goals, then check our commerce programmes for foundation support.

Which finance course has the best scope in 2027?

All three offer scope. Employers now reward professionals who combine qualifications with technology and data skills.

title: CA Intermediate Study Material: What to Use, What to Skip (Subject-wise Guide)
excerpt: Open any CA Intermediate Study Material Telegram group and you will find fifty PDFs, ten test series and a hundred opinions. Most students do not fail because they lack material. description: Confused by CA Intermediate books and notes? See which ICAI study material to use, what to skip and the best resources for each subject.
content:
Open any CA Intermediate Study Material Telegram group and you will find fifty PDFs, ten test series and a hundred opinions. Most students do not fail because they lack material. They fail because they own too much of it.

This guide cuts through the noise. It tells you which resources give you the highest return, which ones you can safely skip and how to combine them for each subject.

The Golden Rule: One Source, Three Passes

Choose one primary source per subject, then revise it three times: first to learn, second to practise and third to retain. Extra resources should fill specific gaps, not replace your primary source. In our experience with CA aspirants, students who follow this rule finish more revision cycles than students who keep switching.

The Core ICAI Study Material

ICAI’s own material remains the foundation, because the examiners set papers from the Institute’s syllabus and approach. You can access it free of cost through ICAI’s Board of Studies (BoS) Knowledge Portal. The following resources matter most:

  • Study modules: Your primary reading and concept source.
  • Practice manuals: Question banks with solutions; essential for numerical subjects.
  • Revision Test Papers (RTPs): Short, chapter-wise questions released before each attempt.
  • Mock Test Papers (MTPs): Full-length papers that mimic the exam.
  • Past papers and suggested answers: Your best guide to question trends and presentation.
  • Statutory updates and amendment notes: Critical for Taxation, Law and Auditing.

Always download the edition meant for your attempt. An outdated PDF can quietly cost you marks.

Subject-wise Guide: What to Use and What to Skip

Advanced Accounting

  • Use: ICAI module, practice manual, past papers
  • Add if needed: One standard reference for Ind AS clarity or extra practice
  • Skip: Multiple question banks that repeat the same sums

Corporate and Other Laws

  • Use: ICAI module, latest amendment notes, RTPs
  • Add if needed: Bare-act extracts for key sections
  • Skip: Lengthy case-law collections that the syllabus does not require

Taxation

  • Use: The edition matching your attempt’s applicable law, ICAI’s statutory update, practice manual
  • Add if needed: A well-organised revision summary of amendments
  • Skip: Old books and unverified “short notes” that ignore recent changes. Taxation moves quickly, so always confirm which provisions ICAI treats as applicable for your attempt.

Cost and Management Accounting

  • Use: ICAI module and practice manual
  • Add if needed: A formula and format sheet you build yourself
  • Skip: Extra theory notes, since the paper is mostly numerical

Auditing and Ethics

  • Use: ICAI module, standards summary, RTPs and MTPs
  • Add if needed: Case-based question practice
  • Skip: Rote summaries without scenarios; examiners test application

Financial Management and Strategic Management

  • Use: ICAI module and practice manual for FM; ICAI module for SM
  • Add if needed: A formula sheet for FM; a keyword sheet for SM
  • Skip: Heavy corporate-strategy textbooks that go beyond the syllabus

How to Judge Any Note, Book or Test Series

Before you buy or download anything, ask four questions:

  1. Is it updated for my attempt? Check the edition date and the applicable law.
  2. Does it follow ICAI’s syllabus? Compare the index with the ICAI module.
  3. Does it add something the ICAI material lacks? If not, skip it.
  4. Can I finish it before the exam? A resource you cannot complete is a distraction.

The Role of Notes

Personal notes beat borrowed notes. Make short notes only after you finish a chapter and solve questions, because you then know what you forget. Keep them to a page per chapter, and update them after every mock test. Borrowed notes can supplement your revision, but they cannot replace your own understanding.

Choosing a Test Series

A test series helps only if you attempt papers on schedule and review them. Look for these features:

  • Papers that follow ICAI’s pattern, marks and time
  • Detailed answers or video discussions
  • A clear schedule that matches your revision plan
  • Evaluation or feedback, not only a marking scheme

Use ICAI’s MTPs as a free baseline and add one external series if you need more practice.

Sample Study Material Stack (Per Subject)

Where Coaching Fits In

Coaching does not replace the ICAI material; it organises it. Good faculty tell you which topics carry weight, which questions repeat and how examiners expect answers to look. EdgeX Learning builds its CA coaching in Mumbai with specialist faculty, comprehensive study material, a practice question bank and regular doubt-solving sessions. If you are still planning your timetable, read our CA Intermediate study plan for January 2027 and then match each resource to its phase.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is ICAI study material enough for CA Intermediate?

For many students, yes, when combined with the practice manual, RTPs, MTPs and past papers. Some subjects, such as Taxation, also need careful tracking of updates.

Where can I download ICAI study material?

ICAI’s Board of Studies Knowledge Portal hosts the modules, RTPs, MTPs and other resources.

Which are the best CA Inter books?

Start with ICAI’s own modules. Add a reference book only when you identify a gap, and choose the edition that matches your attempt.

Are CA Inter notes from other students useful?

They help for quick revision, but only after you have built your own understanding. Verify that they reflect current amendments.

How many mock tests should I attempt?

Aim for at least two full-length papers per subject before the exam, and review each one in detail.

title: ACCA 2027 Changes Explained: New Structure, Exams & What It Means for Indian Students
excerpt: Should you start ACCA now or wait for the new syllabus? That one question fills the inbox of every ACCA tutor in India. The short answer: do not wait. ACCA has built a transition framework that maps your passed exams into the new structure. This guide explains ACCA 2027 changes and how to act. Verification…
description: ACCA’s 2027 qualification moves from 13 to 11 exams with new Knowledge, Expertise and Strategic Professional levels.
content:
Should you start ACCA now or wait for the new syllabus? That one question fills the inbox of every ACCA tutor in India. The short answer: do not wait. ACCA has built a transition framework that maps your passed exams into the new structure. This guide explains ACCA 2027 changes and how to act.

Verification note: ACCA is rolling out details in stages, and training providers describe some specifics slightly differently. Confirm final paper names and dates on ACCA’s official website before you plan your exams.

What Is Changing in the ACCA Qualification?

ACCA’s “Future Ready” redesign reshapes the qualification around employability, technology and ethics. The headline changes reported across multiple providers are:

  • Fewer exams: the main route moves from 13 exams to 11.
  • New level names: Knowledge, Expertise and Strategic Professional replace the current Applied Knowledge, Applied Skills and Strategic Professional labels.
  • Law moves earlier: Corporate and Business Law shifts to the Knowledge level.
  • Simpler options: where students currently choose two optional papers, they will choose one.
  • Employability modules: a new employability component (reported as a Responsible Business Management module at Knowledge level) sits alongside the exams.
  • More data and technology: Performance Management evolves into a paper focused on data analysis, reflecting the profession’s shift.
  • Reference materials: from September 2027, ACCA plans to provide permitted reference materials in Strategic Professional exams.

ACCA 2027 Timeline

New Structure at a Glance

Knowledge Level (K1–K3)

Students will sit three Knowledge papers, reported as K1, K2 and K3, in place of Business and Technology, Management Accounting and Financial Accounting. ACCA recommends taking them in order.

Expertise Level (E1–E5)

This level replaces much of today’s Applied Skills stage, with five papers. One of them, reported as E5, carries a strong data-analysis focus.

Strategic Professional Level

This level continues to build leadership, strategy and advanced reporting, with fewer optional choices and new support such as reference materials.

Will Your Passed Exams Count?

Yes. ACCA has stated that completed exams and exemptions carry over, and it provides a Transition Tool to map your current progress to the new papers. Entry requirements and exemption policies for graduates are reported as unchanged. Therefore, you should never delay a paper just because the syllabus is changing.

What Indian Students Should Do Now

Your action depends on where you stand today.

If You Are Just Starting

Begin with the current structure. Most of your early studying happens before the new syllabus fully applies, and your passes carry across. Starting now also lets you use the existing exemption routes available to eligible commerce graduates.

If You Are Halfway Through

Finish the Applied Skills papers before the June 2027 final sitting if you can. Otherwise, use ACCA’s Transition Tool to see which new papers your passes cover. Many students will study a mix of old and new papers.

If You Are a Commerce Student or CA Aspirant

Understand how ACCA differs from the CA route before you choose. Our guide on CFA vs CA vs ACCA compares them side by side.

Why These Changes Matter for Your Career

Employers increasingly ask for analysts who can read data, question outputs and explain decisions. ACCA’s changes respond to that demand. Because the profession is changing quickly, our article on whether AI will replace accountants shows which skills to build alongside the qualification.

How to Prepare for the Transition

  1. Stay on your current plan. Nothing changes until mid-2027.
  2. Build data skills early. Learn Excel well, then explore Power BI or SQL basics.
  3. Track official updates. Watch ACCA’s website for specimen exams and guidance packs.
  4. Choose a tutor who updates fast. Ask any institute how it will handle the changeover.

Studying ACCA in Mumbai

Mumbai students have many options, so ask direct questions: How will you teach the ACCA 2027 syllabus? How do you track transition mapping? What support do you offer for the new computer-based format? EdgeX Learning provides ACCA coaching in Mumbai with pathway counselling before admission (covering eligibility, exemptions and paper progression), paper-wise preparation and regular doubt-solving sessions. If you are comparing an ACCA course in Mumbai with other options, check each provider’s transition plan first.

Frequently Asked Questions

When does the new ACCA syllabus start?

Reports point to Knowledge-level exams from July 2027 and Expertise and Strategic Professional exams from September 2027, with a final sitting of current Applied Skills and Strategic Professional exams in June 2027.

Is ACCA reducing the number of exams?

Yes. The main route is reported to move from 13 exams to 11.

Will my passed ACCA exams expire?

No. ACCA says your progress maps into the new structure, and it offers a Transition Tool.

Should I join ACCA now or wait until 2027?

Join now. Your passes carry across, and waiting only delays your qualification.

Is ACCA worth it for Indian students in 2027?

It suits students who want global career options in finance, audit, reporting and consulting. Compare it with CA and CFA using our three-way comparison.

Does ACCA include AI and data skills now?

The 2027 redesign adds stronger technology and data content, including a data-analysis-focused paper.

content:
You can lose a CA attempt without writing a single answer. A missed form deadline costs you six months, and it is entirely preventable. This guide gives you the dates, the process and a checklist, so you submit your January 2027 exam form correctly the first time.

Key Dates for the ICAI January 2027 Exam Form

ICAI announced the January 2027 schedule on 23 September 2026. Current reports on the notification confirm the following:

ICAI usually keeps a short correction window open after the form window closes, typically about two days. Do not rely on it, because ICAI decides whether and when to open it. Always confirm every date on ICAI’s official notification, since the Institute can revise schedules.

Who Must Fill the Exam Form?

Every candidate appearing in the January 2027 Foundation or Intermediate exams must submit the form. Before you start, confirm that:

  • your registration for the relevant course is active,
  • you have completed the eligibility and study requirements ICAI sets for your level, and
  • you know whether you will appear in one group or both (for Intermediate).

If you are unsure about eligibility, ask your ICAI regional office or your coaching mentor before you pay any fee.

Step-by-Step: How to Fill the CA Exam Form on SSP

Follow this sequence to avoid errors.

  1. Log in to SSP with your registration number and password. Reset your password early if you have forgotten it.
  2. Open the exam application section and select Foundation or Intermediate.
  3. Choose your group(s) for Intermediate carefully. Changing it later may not be possible.
  4. Select your exam centre. Mumbai is among the 207 cities ICAI has notified for the January 2027 session.
  5. Choose your medium. ICAI offers English and Hindi.
  6. Check your photograph and signature against ICAI’s specifications.
  7. Pay the fee online and wait for the payment confirmation.
  8. Download your submission receipt and keep it safely.

Exam Fees: What You Should Know

ICAI publishes fees by course, number of groups and centre location (for example, different amounts apply to overseas centres). Because fees can change between sessions, we do not quote a figure here. Instead, open the fee table in the official notification or inside SSP before you pay. Budget for a possible late fee if you submit after 16 November.

Exam Centres and Medium

ICAI will hold the January 2027 exams at 207 centres across India, along with overseas centres in Bahrain, Dubai and Kathmandu. Mumbai students normally have several centre options. Choose the centre closest to your home, and check travel time at 2 PM on a weekday, because afternoon traffic in Mumbai can add 30–45 minutes. Our experience with students in the city suggests that candidates who rehearse the commute arrive calmer and write better.

The Complete Pre-Submission Checklist

Tick each item before you press “Submit”:

  • Registration is valid and your login works
  • Group choice (Intermediate) is final
  • Centre and medium are selected
  • Photo and signature meet ICAI’s specifications
  • Fee payment is complete and the receipt is saved
  • Contact number and email are correct, because ICAI sends updates there
  • You have set reminders for the form deadline and for the admit card release

Common Mistakes to Avoid

  • Waiting for the last day. Portals slow down when thousands of candidates log in together.

What to Do Right After Submitting the Form

Frequently Asked Questions

When does the CA January 2027 exam form start?

The application window opens on 3 November 2026 at 10 AM on ICAI’s Self Service Portal.

What is the last date to fill the CA exam form for January 2027?

Reports based on ICAI’s notification give 16 November 2026 as the last date without a late fee. A late-fee window may follow.

Is there a correction window after the form closes?

ICAI has usually opened one for about two days. Confirm on the portal, because it is not guaranteed.

Can I choose Mumbai as my exam centre?

Yes. Mumbai is on ICAI’s list of notified cities for January 2027.

Is the CA Final schedule included?

No. This notification covers Foundation and Intermediate only. Watch ICAI’s website for any CA Final announcement.

In which languages can I write the exam?

English and Hindi.

content:
Preparing for CA Intermediate can feel overwhelming when you have to manage multiple subjects, lengthy chapters and regular practice at the same time. The challenge becomes even greater for students appearing for both groups in the January 2027 attempt.

The solution is not simply to increase your study hours. You need a realistic timetable that balances syllabus coverage, numerical practice, theory revision and mock tests.

With the examinations scheduled to begin in January 2027, students starting their focused preparation on 25 October have approximately 10 weeks before the first examination. This period needs to be used carefully, especially if you are preparing for both groups.

This guide explains how to prepare for CA Intermediate January 2027 with a week-wise study plan, subject-specific strategies and practical tips for managing multiple subjects without losing track of revision.

CA Intermediate January 2027 Exam Dates

Before preparing your timetable, keep the announced examination schedule in mind.

According to the timetable referenced for the January 2027 attempt:

  • Group I: 2, 4 and 6 January 2027
  • Group II: 8, 10 and 12 January 2027
  • Examination timing: 2 PM onwards, as specified in the announced schedule
  • Duration: Three hours per paper, according to the schedule referenced here

Check the official ICAI website for the latest examination notifications, applicable syllabus, admit card details and any changes to the timetable.

Students should also check the applicable examination form deadline and submission requirements through ICAI’s official channels. Complete registration and administrative tasks within the prescribed window rather than leaving them until the final weeks.

Understand the Six CA Intermediate Subjects

Before building a CA Inter study timetable, understand which subjects require numerical practice, conceptual understanding or repeated revision.

Group I

  1. Advanced Accounting: Requires conceptual clarity, numerical accuracy and extensive question practice.
  2. Corporate and Other Laws: Requires an understanding of legal provisions, amendments and application-based answers.
  3. Taxation: Covers Income Tax and GST, with an emphasis on concepts, computations and applicable statutory updates.

Group II

  1. Cost and Management Accounting: Requires familiarity with costing methods, formulas and problem-solving techniques.
  2. Auditing and Ethics: Requires conceptual understanding, accurate terminology and structured answers.
  3. Financial Management and Strategic Management: Combines numerical problem-solving in Financial Management with conceptual learning and recall in Strategic Management.

The ideal study routine should include practice-heavy subjects throughout the week while reserving regular sessions for theory and revision.

Should You Prepare for One Group or Both?

Your preparation strategy should depend on how much of the syllabus you have already covered and how consistently you can study.

Preparing for Both Groups

Preparing for both groups may suit students who have completed a substantial portion of the syllabus and can maintain a demanding study schedule.

Consider both groups if you can:

  • Revise the majority of the syllabus before the final revision phase.
  • Commit sufficient daily study time without sacrificing sleep and concentration.
  • Practise questions across all six subjects.
  • Complete mock tests and analyse your mistakes.
  • Keep up with relevant amendments and statutory updates.

Preparing for One Group

A single-group strategy may be more suitable if you still have major syllabus gaps or need more time to understand difficult subjects.

It allows you to concentrate on three subjects, practise more questions and revise more thoroughly before the examinations.

The right decision depends on your preparation level, not simply the number of subjects you want to complete. A realistic plan that matches your current progress is more useful than an ambitious timetable that you cannot sustain.

How to Manage Multiple Subjects in CA Intermediate

One of the biggest challenges is retaining information across six subjects without neglecting the chapters that require regular practice.

A useful approach is the 2 + 1 subject rotation. Each day, focus on two major subjects and one shorter revision or theory session.

For example:

  • Practice-heavy subject: Advanced Accounting, Taxation, Cost and Management Accounting, or Financial Management.
  • Theory and application subject: Corporate and Other Laws or Auditing and Ethics.
  • Revision subject: Strategic Management, formulas, legal provisions or previously incorrect questions.

Rotate the subjects throughout the week so that every paper receives regular attention.

For students preparing for both groups, a sample day might include two hours of Advanced Accounting, two hours of Taxation and one hour of Law revision, followed by additional question practice or a mock-test review.

This is a flexible framework, not a mandatory daily schedule. Adjust the time allocation according to your syllabus completion and subject-wise performance.

CA Intermediate Study Plan for January 2027: Week-Wise Schedule

Starting on 25 October 2026, divide your preparation into syllabus coverage, intensive practice, revision and final exam preparation.

The schedule below is designed to help you organise the remaining preparation period without relying on an outdated 75-day countdown.

Weeks 1–2: 25 October–7 November — Assess Your Preparation and Cover Key Chapters

Begin by reviewing your syllabus and identifying the chapters you have completed, partially completed or not started.

During these two weeks:

  • Create a separate checklist for all six subjects.
  • Prioritise difficult and practice-intensive chapters.
  • Study Advanced Accounting and Cost and Management Accounting regularly.
  • Start or continue Taxation computations and GST practice.
  • Revise important provisions in Corporate and Other Laws.
  • Build concise notes for Auditing and Strategic Management.
  • Solve ICAI study material questions after completing each topic.

Students preparing for both groups should distribute their study hours across all six subjects. Single-group candidates can allocate more time to their three selected subjects.

Weekly target: Establish a realistic timetable, identify weak areas and make consistent progress with syllabus coverage.

Weeks 3–4: 8–21 November — Complete Syllabus Coverage and Strengthen Concepts

Use this phase to work towards completing your first pass through the syllabus.

Focus on:

  • Completing the remaining important chapters.
  • Solving chapter-wise questions in numerical subjects.
  • Practising case-based questions in Law and Audit.
  • Revising Taxation concepts alongside computation questions.
  • Reviewing formulas and common costing techniques.
  • Preparing concise Strategic Management notes.
  • Taking short tests to identify concepts that need further attention.

Avoid leaving all theory subjects until the final weeks. Regular revision helps you retain information while continuing with the remaining syllabus.

If you are significantly behind, prioritise essential topics and make a clear plan to address the remaining gaps.

Weekly target: Complete as much of the planned syllabus as possible and establish a consistent question-practice routine.

Weeks 5–6: 22 November–5 December — Chapter-Wise Practice and Error Correction

At this stage, preparation should become more question-oriented.

Your priorities should include:

  • Solving chapter-wise tests for all your selected subjects.
  • Practising relevant previous examination questions.
  • Using ICAI’s applicable practice resources and revision material.
  • Reworking difficult Accounting, Taxation, Costing and FM questions.
  • Writing structured answers for Law and Audit.
  • Testing recall in Strategic Management.
  • Maintaining an error log for conceptual, calculation and presentation mistakes.

After each test, identify why you lost marks. If the issue is a conceptual gap, revisit the topic. If it is a calculation error, practise similar questions. If your answer lacks structure, work on presentation.

Weekly target: Improve question-solving ability and identify the topics that require additional revision.

Weeks 7–8: 6–19 December — First Full Revision and Timed Practice

Begin a structured revision cycle across your selected subjects.

During these weeks:

  • Revise important concepts using short notes.
  • Revisit questions previously answered incorrectly.
  • Practise numerical problems under time limits.
  • Review applicable Taxation amendments and statutory updates.
  • Revise important legal provisions and auditing concepts.
  • Practise Strategic Management recall through short questions.
  • Attempt timed papers or substantial mock-test sections.

Students preparing for both groups should maintain a balanced revision schedule. Do not devote all your time to Group I while allowing Group II subjects to become unfamiliar.

Weekly target: Complete a substantial revision cycle and improve accuracy through timed practice.

Week 9: 20–26 December — Mock Tests and Weak-Area Improvement

This week should focus on testing your preparation under realistic examination conditions.

Plan to:

  • Attempt timed mock papers based on the applicable examination pattern.
  • Practise at the scheduled examination time where possible.
  • Analyse each paper after completing it.
  • Identify chapters where your performance remains weak.
  • Revise important formulas, provisions and concepts.
  • Rework recurring mistakes rather than simply reading their solutions.

Students appearing for both groups should practise papers from both groups. Single-group candidates should devote their mock-test time to their selected group.

Do not judge your preparation only by mock-test scores. Use the results to identify what needs to change before the examination.

Weekly target: Improve examination readiness and address the most important remaining weaknesses.

Week 10: 27 December–1 January — Final Revision and Exam Readiness

The final days before Group I require a focused approach. Avoid starting multiple new resources or attempting to learn every difficult topic from scratch.

For Group I candidates:

  • Revise Advanced Accounting questions, formats and important concepts.
  • Review key provisions and application-based questions in Law.
  • Practise selected Taxation computations.
  • Review your error log and concise notes.
  • Check your admit card and examination arrangements.
  • Maintain a regular sleep schedule.

For students appearing for both groups, continue short, structured revision sessions for Group II. Do not abandon Costing, Audit or FM and SM entirely while focusing on Group I.

For Group II-only candidates, use this period for full Group II revision and timed practice, while following the announced examination schedule.

Weekly target: Consolidate your preparation, reduce avoidable errors and enter the examination period with a clear plan.

2–12 January — Follow the Examination Schedule

Students appearing for both groups need to manage the short interval between the two groups carefully.

After completing a Group I paper, avoid spending excessive time discussing answers or comparing attempts with other students. Shift your attention to the next scheduled paper.

After the Group I examinations conclude on 6 January, use 7 January for focused revision of Cost and Management Accounting, as applicable to your preparation needs, before the Group II examination on 8 January.

Continue with the remaining Group II papers according to the official timetable.

The interval between groups is too short for a complete revision from scratch. This is why Group II revision must already be well advanced before January begins.

Subject-Wise CA Intermediate Preparation Strategy

1. Advanced Accounting

Advanced Accounting requires regular numerical practice and a strong understanding of the applicable accounting standards and syllabus topics.

  • Solve questions from ICAI study material.
  • Practise complete solutions rather than memorising final answers.
  • Revise important formats and working notes.
  • Rework questions where you repeatedly make calculation errors.
  • Practise relevant previous examination questions.

Prioritise accuracy and clear presentation. Avoid spending all your time on familiar chapters while leaving important syllabus areas untouched.

2. Corporate and Other Laws

Law preparation requires more than reading provisions repeatedly. You must understand their meaning and apply them correctly to the question.

  • Revise relevant provisions and legal concepts.
  • Follow applicable amendments and official study updates.
  • Practise case-based questions.
  • Structure answers using the issue, relevant provision, application and conclusion.
  • Test your recall without looking at your notes.

Short, frequent revision sessions can help you retain provisions more effectively than leaving the subject untouched for several days.

3. Taxation

Taxation requires conceptual understanding, regular computations and attention to the provisions applicable to your examination attempt.

  • Practise Income Tax and GST questions consistently.
  • Maintain separate revision notes for each area.
  • Review the applicable statutory amendments and ICAI updates.
  • Practise complete computations and check your working.
  • Revisit questions where you misapplied a provision or calculation method.

Always confirm which provisions and statutory updates apply to the January 2027 attempt through the relevant ICAI material.

4. Cost and Management Accounting

Costing becomes easier to manage when you understand the logic behind each method instead of memorising formulas in isolation.

  • Revise formulas and standard formats.
  • Practise different question types from the prescribed material.
  • Identify what the question is asking before starting calculations.
  • Check units, assumptions and intermediate workings.
  • Maintain a list of recurring mistakes for revision.

Regular practice is particularly important for improving speed and accuracy in numerical subjects.

5. Auditing and Ethics

Auditing requires conceptual clarity, precise terminology and structured answers.

  • Prepare concise notes for important standards and concepts.
  • Understand the reasoning behind audit procedures.
  • Practise case-based questions.
  • Use headings and logical answer structures.
  • Revisit difficult topics during each revision cycle.

Avoid relying entirely on last-minute memorisation. Understanding the concepts makes it easier to apply them to unfamiliar questions.

6. Financial Management and Strategic Management

These two areas benefit from different study techniques.

Financial Management

  • Practise numerical questions regularly.
  • Revise formulas and their applications.
  • Work through relevant topics such as ratios, leverage and capital budgeting.
  • Review calculation errors and improve time management.

Strategic Management

  • Understand concepts before memorising key terms.
  • Prepare concise notes and comparison tables.
  • Practise recalling important points without referring to the textbook.
  • Revise regularly rather than leaving the entire subject until the final week.

A balanced routine should include FM problem-solving and short Strategic Management revision sessions throughout the preparation period.

Build a Daily CA Inter Study Timetable You Can Follow

A practical timetable should account for your current preparation, coaching or college schedule and the subjects that need the most attention.

Here is a sample routine for students preparing for both groups:

This adds up to approximately 7.5 hours of focused study. Students preparing for both groups may need additional time depending on their progress, while single-group candidates can use the extra time for deeper practice and revision.

To make the timetable sustainable:

  • Study your most demanding subject when you are most alert.
  • Use focused study blocks with short breaks.
  • Revise important formulas and definitions daily.
  • Reserve time every week for tests.
  • Keep one flexible session for unfinished topics.
  • Review your progress at the end of each week.

The best timetable is one you can follow consistently and adjust when your performance shows that a subject needs more attention.

Why Mock Tests Matter for CA Intermediate

Mock tests help you evaluate more than your theoretical knowledge. They also show whether you can manage time, interpret questions correctly and present complete answers under examination conditions.

Whenever possible, practise full papers at 2 PM to familiarise yourself with the scheduled examination time.

After each test, review:

  • Conceptual errors: Did you misunderstand the topic or apply the wrong method?
  • Calculation errors: Did you make avoidable mistakes in numerical questions?
  • Presentation errors: Were your workings or written answers unclear?
  • Time-management errors: Did you spend too long on one question?
  • Revision gaps: Did you forget a provision, formula or key concept?

Use ICAI’s applicable mock test papers, revision resources and previous examination papers as part of your preparation.

For a more efficient approach to selecting resources, read our guide to CA Intermediate study material, which explains how to prioritise useful materials instead of collecting unnecessary references.

When Does CA Intermediate Coaching Help?

Some students can prepare independently with ICAI study material, a clear timetable and regular self-assessment. Others benefit from structured classes, faculty guidance, doubt-solving sessions and feedback on their answers.

EdgeX Learning offers CA coaching in Mumbai with subject-wise faculty support, practice questions, revision sessions and doubt-solving assistance.

Students who need help with difficult concepts, Taxation preparation, Law interpretation or timed question practice can explore the programme to understand whether structured coaching fits their learning needs.

If you are preparing for the CA journey from the beginning, our CA Foundation study plan for January 2027 provides a starting point for understanding the preparation approach at the Foundation level.

Frequently Asked Questions

1. How many hours should I study daily for CA Intermediate?

Your study hours depend on whether you are preparing for one group or both, how much of the syllabus you have completed and how quickly you understand the concepts. Students preparing for both groups may need a more intensive schedule. Focus on completing planned topics, practising questions and revising consistently rather than relying only on a fixed number of hours.

2. Can I clear both groups in January 2027?

It may be possible if you have covered a substantial portion of the syllabus, can devote sufficient time to preparation and complete effective revision and mock tests. If you have significant syllabus gaps, consider whether concentrating on one group would allow you to prepare more thoroughly. No timetable can guarantee a passing result.

3. Which CA Intermediate subject should I study first?

Start with a subject that requires regular practice, such as Advanced Accounting, Taxation, Cost and Management Accounting or Financial Management. However, do not ignore theory subjects. Rotate your subjects throughout the week so that all your selected papers receive consistent attention.

4. Can I prepare for CA Intermediate without coaching?

Yes. ICAI study material provides the foundation for self-study. Students who can maintain a disciplined routine, solve questions independently and evaluate their mistakes may prepare without coaching. A test series or coaching support can be useful if you need additional structure or feedback.

5. What are the CA Intermediate January 2027 exam dates?

The timetable referenced in this guide lists Group I examinations on 2, 4 and 6 January 2027 and Group II examinations on 8, 10 and 12 January 2027. Confirm the dates and examination instructions on ICAI’s official website before finalising your plans.

6. How should I revise Taxation for CA Intermediate?

Use a structured revision approach: review the concepts, practise computation questions, revisit incorrect answers and study the statutory updates applicable to your attempt. Keep separate notes for Income Tax and GST and check ICAI’s official guidance for the relevant syllabus and amendments.

7. When should I start taking mock tests?

Start chapter-wise tests as soon as you have studied the relevant topics. Move towards timed papers as your syllabus coverage improves, and reserve the final preparation weeks for mock tests, performance analysis and targeted revision.

Final Thoughts

A successful CA Intermediate preparation strategy depends on consistency, realistic planning and regular self-assessment. With the January 2027 examinations approaching, use the weeks from 25 October to organise your syllabus coverage, strengthen difficult subjects and establish a reliable revision routine.

If you are preparing for both groups, keep all six subjects active and complete Group II revision before the examinations begin. If you are attempting one group, use the available time to strengthen your selected subjects and practise under examination conditions.

Avoid constantly changing resources or creating unrealistic daily targets. Review your progress every week, correct recurring mistakes and adjust your study timetable according to your actual performance.

A well-planned routine will help you use your remaining preparation time more effectively and approach the examination with greater confidence.

content:
If you are preparing for the CA Foundation January 2027 attempt, now is the time to turn your preparation into a structured routine. With the examinations scheduled to begin on 3 January 2027, students starting on 25 October have approximately 10 weeks to revise the syllabus, practise questions and build exam confidence.

The biggest challenge at this stage is not finding more study material. It is deciding what to study each week, how much time to give each subject and when to start solving mock papers.

Many students spend too much time planning and collecting resources before beginning serious preparation. A better approach is to follow a realistic schedule, practise regularly and review your mistakes instead of repeatedly changing your strategy.

This guide explains how to prepare for CA Foundation January 2027 with a practical 10-week study plan, paper-wise preparation tips and a revision strategy that can help you make the most of the time available.

CA Foundation January 2027: Important Dates at a Glance

Before creating your study timetable, understand the examination schedule and keep track of the relevant ICAI announcements.

  • Examination dates: 3, 5, 7 and 9 January 2027
  • Examination start time: 2 PM, according to the announced timetable
  • Papers: Accounting, Business Laws, Business Mathematics, Logical Reasoning and Statistics, and Business Economics and Business & Commercial Knowledge
  • Exam form window: Scheduled to open on 3 November 2026, as per the announced information
  • Exam centres: Mumbai is among the notified examination locations

Check the official ICAI website for the latest examination notifications, registration requirements, admit card announcements and any changes to the schedule.

Students should also review the examination form instructions and complete the application process within the prescribed window. Do not leave administrative tasks until the final week of preparation.

Understand the Four CA Foundation Papers

Before dividing your time, understand the nature of each paper. A balanced CA Foundation exam strategy should account for the different skills required across all four subjects.

Paper 1: Accounting

Accounting is a subjective paper that requires conceptual understanding, numerical accuracy and regular written practice.

Reading solved examples alone is not enough. Practise journal entries, ledger accounts, financial statements and other syllabus-based questions by hand. Pay attention to formats, calculations and working notes.

Paper 2: Business Laws

Business Laws requires a clear understanding of legal provisions and the ability to apply them to practical situations.

Focus on understanding the concepts before memorising key provisions. Practise writing structured answers that explain the relevant principle, apply it to the situation and reach a clear conclusion.

Paper 3: Business Mathematics, Logical Reasoning and Statistics

This objective paper tests your ability to solve questions accurately within a limited time.

Regular numerical practice is essential. Work on formulas, calculation speed, logical reasoning patterns and statistical concepts. Timed practice can help you identify which questions to attempt first.

Paper 4: Business Economics and Business & Commercial Knowledge

This paper requires conceptual clarity, regular revision and effective recall.

Read the prescribed study material carefully and practise multiple-choice questions. Comparison tables, concise notes and regular self-tests can make it easier to distinguish between similar concepts.

ICAI’s examination scheme and marking instructions should always be checked against the latest official guidance, including the applicable passing criteria and negative-marking rules.

How to Prepare for CA Foundation January 2027: The 10-Week Study Plan

Starting on 25 October 2026, you can divide your preparation into four stages: syllabus coverage, question practice, revision and final exam preparation.

The following schedule provides a practical framework. Adjust the workload according to how much of the syllabus you have already completed.

Weeks 1–2: 25 October–7 November — Assess and Cover Important Concepts

Use the first two weeks to establish a clear picture of your preparation level and cover important concepts across all four papers.

Your priorities should be:

  • Review the syllabus and identify completed, partially completed and untouched chapters.
  • Study Accounting and Business Mathematics regularly because both benefit from consistent practice.
  • Cover Business Laws and Economics through focused reading and short revision sessions.
  • Solve illustrations and questions from ICAI study material alongside each topic.
  • Prepare concise formula sheets, definitions and chapter summaries.
  • Take short topic-wise tests to identify gaps early.

Avoid spending several days designing a perfect timetable. Create a manageable routine and begin studying immediately.

Weekly target: Establish a consistent study schedule and make measurable progress across all four papers.

Weeks 3–4: 8–21 November — Strengthen Syllabus Coverage

During these weeks, continue covering the remaining syllabus while revisiting the concepts studied earlier.

Focus on:

  • Completing the planned chapters in each subject.
  • Solving chapter-wise questions after studying a topic.
  • Practising Accounting problems in writing rather than only reading solutions.
  • Revising legal provisions and practising application-based answers.
  • Solving Mathematics, Logical Reasoning and Statistics MCQs under time limits.
  • Creating a list of difficult questions and recurring mistakes.

By the end of this phase, you should have a clear idea of which chapters require more practice and which topics you can answer confidently.

Weekly target: Make substantial progress towards completing the first pass of the syllabus without neglecting revision.

Weeks 5–6: 22 November–5 December — Finish the First Pass and Begin Intensive Practice

This is the transition from learning concepts to applying them under examination conditions.

Prioritise the following activities:

  • Complete the remaining syllabus wherever possible.
  • Attempt chapter-wise tests for all four papers.
  • Solve relevant previous examination questions and revision questions.
  • Practise full written solutions for Accounting and Business Laws.
  • Use timed sessions for Mathematics, Logical Reasoning and Statistics.
  • Revise Economics concepts through MCQs and short notes.
  • Maintain an error log containing incorrect answers, the reason for each mistake and the correct approach.

Do not postpone testing until you feel completely prepared. Tests are part of the learning process and help you identify weaknesses while there is still time to address them.

Weekly target: Complete syllabus coverage as far as possible and establish a regular testing routine.

Weeks 7–8: 6–19 December — Revision and Mock Tests

At this stage, your focus should shift towards improving accuracy, speed and retention.

Plan your preparation around these tasks:

  • Revise each paper using concise notes and marked questions.
  • Attempt timed mock tests or full-length papers according to the official examination pattern.
  • Analyse your performance after every test.
  • Revisit chapters where you consistently lose marks.
  • Practise MCQs daily for the objective papers.
  • Rework difficult Accounting problems and practise structured Business Laws answers.
  • Revise formulas, definitions and important distinctions regularly.

Do not measure progress only by the number of hours spent studying. Track the questions you can solve correctly, the mistakes you have eliminated and the topics you can recall without referring to your notes.

Weekly target: Complete your first serious round of revision and use test results to guide further study.

Week 9: 20–26 December — Strengthen Weak Areas

The ninth week is for targeted improvement rather than starting multiple new resources.

Use your mock-test results and error log to decide what needs attention.

  • Revisit frequently tested syllabus concepts using official material.
  • Solve questions from chapters where your accuracy is low.
  • Practise calculations and written answers under time limits.
  • Revise formulas and key legal provisions.
  • Review recurring errors instead of repeatedly solving only familiar questions.
  • Attempt additional timed papers if your preparation level allows.

If you have not completed the entire syllabus, prioritise completing essential topics while retaining enough time for revision. Avoid making unrealistic promises to yourself about finishing everything in a single day.

Weekly target: Improve weak areas and reduce avoidable mistakes.

Week 10: 27 December–2 January — Final Revision and Exam Readiness

The final week should be organised, focused and manageable. Avoid changing your entire preparation strategy at this stage.

Your priorities should include:

  • Revise short notes, formulas and important concepts.
  • Review previously incorrect questions.
  • Practise selected MCQs and numerical questions.
  • Check examination instructions and admit card details.
  • Confirm your examination centre and travel arrangements.
  • Maintain regular sleep and meal timings.
  • Avoid exhausting yourself with repeated full-length tests immediately before the examination.

Since the examinations begin at 2 PM, practise maintaining concentration during the afternoon. Enter the examination period with a clear plan rather than trying to learn large amounts of new material at the last minute.

Weekly target: Retain what you have studied, stay composed and prepare for the examination environment.

Paper-Wise CA Foundation Study Tips

A common preparation mistake is giving every subject the same type of attention. Each paper requires a slightly different approach.

1. Accounting: Practise by Writing

Start by strengthening your understanding of basic accounting concepts and the relevant syllabus topics.

Follow these steps:

  • Work through ICAI illustrations before attempting more challenging questions.
  • Practise complete solutions, including formats and working notes.
  • Rework questions you answered incorrectly.
  • Maintain a list of common calculation errors.
  • Set aside regular time for numerical practice.

Presentation and accurate workings can make your answers clearer and help you avoid losing marks through avoidable mistakes.

2. Business Laws: Understand and Apply

Reading provisions repeatedly without testing your understanding can create a false sense of preparation.

Use a structured approach when practising application-based questions:

  1. Identify the relevant legal principle.
  2. Explain the applicable provision or concept.
  3. Apply it to the facts given in the question.
  4. State a clear conclusion.

Practise writing answers in your own words while preserving the legal meaning. Regular written practice can improve both recall and answer structure.

3. Business Mathematics, Logical Reasoning and Statistics: Improve Speed and Accuracy

These subjects require repeated practice rather than passive reading.

  • Revise formulas regularly.
  • Practise questions in short, timed sessions.
  • Identify calculation-heavy topics that need additional work.
  • Review incorrect answers to understand the underlying concept.
  • Attempt easier questions first when this suits the examination instructions and your strategy.

Accuracy should come before speed. Once you understand the methods, timed practice can help you work more efficiently.

4. Business Economics and Business & Commercial Knowledge: Revise Consistently

Avoid leaving these subjects entirely for the final week.

Read the prescribed material, make concise notes and practise MCQs throughout your preparation. Use comparison tables for similar concepts and revisit incorrect answers to improve retention.

Short, frequent revision sessions can be more effective than trying to memorise everything in one sitting.

How Many Hours Should You Study Daily?

The right number of hours depends on your current preparation level, available time and familiarity with the syllabus.

As a starting point, consider five to six focused hours on regular study days, increasing your study time when necessary and manageable. Students with significant portions of the syllabus remaining may need a more intensive schedule.

A sample daily routine could look like this:

This is an example, not a fixed rule. Rotate the sessions according to your strengths and weaknesses, and include appropriate breaks.

If you attend college or coaching classes, plan your self-study around those commitments rather than following a timetable that is difficult to sustain.

Five Mistakes to Avoid During CA Foundation Preparation

1. Studying One Subject for Too Long Without Revising Others

Focusing on a single paper for several days can leave other subjects neglected. Rotate subjects regularly to maintain familiarity with the entire syllabus.

2. Ignoring Written Practice

Reading solved answers does not provide the same experience as solving them independently. Practise numerical questions and subjective answers on paper.

3. Collecting Too Many Study Resources

Switching between multiple books, PDFs and video courses wastes valuable time. Use the prescribed ICAI material as your foundation and add resources only when they address a specific learning gap.

4. Delaying Mock Tests

Waiting until the syllabus feels perfect before attempting tests can leave you unprepared for time pressure. Begin with chapter-wise tests and progress towards timed papers as your preparation improves.

5. Revising Without Reviewing Mistakes

Simply repeating familiar questions may not improve your score. Record errors, understand why they happened and solve similar questions again to check whether you have corrected the problem.

How Structured Guidance Can Help

Self-study can work well for students who are disciplined, understand the syllabus and can evaluate their own performance. However, some students benefit from a structured timetable, regular assessments and guidance when they struggle with difficult concepts.

EdgeX Learning offers CA coaching in Mumbai, with centres in Borivali and Andheri. Its learning support includes faculty guidance, practice questions, doubt-solving sessions and revision lectures.

Students who prefer a more structured preparation routine can explore the institute’s CA classes in Mumbai to understand the programme and available support before making a decision.

If you are planning beyond Foundation, you can also explore a CA Intermediate study plan for the relevant examination attempt and learn how the preparation requirements change at the next level.

Frequently Asked Questions

1. Is 10 weeks enough to prepare for CA Foundation January 2027?

Ten weeks can be sufficient for some students, particularly those who have already covered a substantial part of the syllabus. Students starting from scratch will need to prioritise carefully, study consistently and devote sufficient time to question practice and revision. No study plan can guarantee a passing result.

2. How should I start preparing for CA Foundation on 25 October 2026?

Begin by reviewing the syllabus, assessing your current preparation and creating a weekly timetable. Start studying all four papers, practise questions alongside each topic and schedule regular revision. Avoid spending the first few days collecting resources instead of studying.

3. How many hours should I study daily for CA Foundation?

The required study time depends on your preparation level and daily commitments. Five to six focused hours can be a useful starting point for a student following a structured plan, but some students may need more or less time. Focus on syllabus coverage, accuracy and regular revision rather than hours alone.

4. Which CA Foundation paper is the most difficult?

There is no universally hardest paper. Students who are comfortable with calculations may find numerical subjects more manageable, while others may need more time for Accounting, Business Laws or Economics. Identify your weaker areas through practice tests and allocate your time accordingly.

5. Is there negative marking in CA Foundation?

Negative marking has applied to objective papers under the CA Foundation examination scheme. However, students should verify the latest ICAI examination instructions for the applicable attempt before deciding how to approach uncertain MCQs.

6. What are the CA Foundation January 2027 exam dates?

According to the announced timetable referenced in this guide, the examinations are scheduled for 3, 5, 7 and 9 January 2027. Check ICAI’s official website for the latest notifications before making final arrangements.

7. Should I join CA Foundation coaching or study independently?

Both approaches can work. Self-study may suit students who can follow a schedule, understand concepts independently and assess their performance. Coaching may help students who need structured classes, regular tests, doubt-solving support or faculty feedback. Choose according to your learning needs and available resources.

Final Thoughts

Preparing for CA Foundation January 2027 requires a realistic plan, consistent effort and regular evaluation. Starting on 25 October gives you a defined period to work through the syllabus, practise questions, revise key concepts and improve your examination technique.

Use the 10-week schedule as a guide rather than a rigid rule. If you are ahead, devote more time to mock tests and weak areas. If you are behind, prioritise essential syllabus coverage and make sure revision does not disappear from your timetable.

Most importantly, begin today, monitor your progress every week and make adjustments based on your actual performance. A focused and sustainable routine is more valuable than a perfect timetable that you never follow.
